Ibn Kathir says: Allah, exalted is He, informs that He is the Creator of what is in the heavens and the earth, and of what lies between them of things, and that He is the Owner of the dominion, the one who disposes of it. In His hand He alternates the night and the day.

﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾. That is, He subjected them, both running in succession, neither of them ceasing, each one seeking the other eagerly, like His saying: ﴿He covers the night over the day, which pursues it swiftly﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. This is the meaning of what has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾. That is, until a known period with Allah, after which they will cease on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Almighty, the Forgiving﴾. That is, despite His might, greatness and majesty, He is Forgiving to whoever disobeys Him, then repents and turns back to Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾. That is, He created you, despite the difference of your kinds, categories, languages and colours, from a single soul, and it is Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾, and she is Eve, peace be upon them both, like His saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women﴾ [an-Nisa: 1].

* *

His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock eight mates﴾. That is, He created for you from the backs of the livestock eight mates, which are those mentioned in Surat al-An'am: ﴿eight mates: two of the sheep and two of the goats﴾ [al-An'am: 143], ﴿and two of the camels and two of the cattle﴾ [al-An'am: 144].

* *

His saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾. That is, He shapes you in the wombs of your mothers, ﴿creation after creation﴾: one of you is first a drop (nutfah), then becomes a clot (‘alaqah), then becomes a lump of flesh (mudghah), then is formed so that he becomes flesh, bone, sinew and veins, and the spirit is breathed into him, so he becomes another creation. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14].

* *

His saying: ﴿In three darknesses﴾. This means: the darkness of the womb, the darkness of the placenta (al-mashimah) — which is like a covering and a shield over the child — and the darkness of the belly. Thus said Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd [and others].

* *

His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾. That is: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and created you and created your fathers, is the Lord; to Him belong the dominion and the disposal of all of that. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, that is, the One to whom worship is due alone. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ That is: how then do you worship other than Him alongside Him? Where do your minds go?!

Ibn Kathir says: Allah, exalted is He, informs that He is the Creator of what is in the heavens and the earth, and of what lies between them of things, and that He is the Owner of the dominion, the one who disposes of it. In His hand He alternates the night and the day.

﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾. That is, He subjected them, both running in succession, neither of them ceasing, each one seeking the other eagerly, like His saying: ﴿He covers the night over the day, which pursues it swiftly﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. This is the meaning of what has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾. That is, until a known period with Allah, after which they will cease on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Almighty, the Forgiving﴾. That is, despite His might, greatness and majesty, He is Forgiving to whoever disobeys Him, then repents and turns back to Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾. That is, He created you, despite the difference of your kinds, categories, languages and colours, from a single soul, and it is Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾, and she is Eve, peace be upon them both, like His saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women﴾ [an-Nisa: 1].

* *

His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock eight mates﴾. That is, He created for you from the backs of the livestock eight mates, which are those mentioned in Surat al-An'am: ﴿eight mates: two of the sheep and two of the goats﴾ [al-An'am: 143], ﴿and two of the camels and two of the cattle﴾ [al-An'am: 144].

* *

His saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾. That is, He shapes you in the wombs of your mothers, ﴿creation after creation﴾: one of you is first a drop (nutfah), then becomes a clot (‘alaqah), then becomes a lump of flesh (mudghah), then is formed so that he becomes flesh, bone, sinew and veins, and the spirit is breathed into him, so he becomes another creation. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14].

* *

His saying: ﴿In three darknesses﴾. This means: the darkness of the womb, the darkness of the placenta (al-mashimah) — which is like a covering and a shield over the child — and the darkness of the belly. Thus said Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd [and others].

* *

His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾. That is: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and created you and created your fathers, is the Lord; to Him belong the dominion and the disposal of all of that. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, that is, the One to whom worship is due alone. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ That is: how then do you worship other than Him alongside Him? Where do your minds go?!

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, reporting about Himself, may He be exalted: that He is (Al-Ghani) the One free of need from all creation, as Musa (Moses) said: ﴿If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth altogether, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrahim 14:8].

In Sahih Muslim: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of a man among you, that would not decrease anything of My dominion."[[Sahih Muslim, no. 2577, from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

* *

His saying ﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ means He does not love it and does not command it. ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ means He loves it from you and increases you from His bounty.

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ means no soul bears anything on behalf of another soul; rather, each one is held accountable for its own affair. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ means nothing hidden from Him is concealed.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾ means that in time of need he humbles himself and seeks help from Allah alone, having no partner, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke fade away except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away, and man is ever ungrateful﴾ [Al-Isra 17:67]. Therefore He said: ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before﴾ means that in a state of ease he forgets that supplication and humility, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing. But when We remove his harm, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us for harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus 10:12].

﴿And he sets up rivals to Allah to mislead [others] from His way﴾ means that in a state of well-being he associates others with Allah and makes rivals for Him. ﴿Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."﴾ means: say to one whose state, way, and course is this: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little." This is a severe threat and a firm warning, like His saying: ﴿Say, "Enjoy yourselves, for indeed your destination is the Fire"﴾ [Ibrahim 14:30], and His saying: ﴿We give them enjoyment for a little, then We will force them to a harsh punishment﴾ [Luqman 31:24].

Allah says: Is one who is like this (who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing) like one who associates partners with Allah and sets up rivals to Him? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. Just as Allah said: ﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is an upright community who recite the verses of Allah during the night hours while they prostrate﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 113]. Here He said: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing﴾, meaning: during his prostration and during his standing.

For this reason, those who hold that qunut (devout obedience) in prayer is humility (khushu') in prayer, and not standing alone, as others have held, derive their evidence from this verse.

Al-Thawri narrated from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The qani't is the one who obeys Allah and His Messenger."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿hours of the night﴾: "the middle of the night." Al-Thawri narrated from Mansur: "We have been told that it refers to the time between Maghrib and 'Isha'."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said regarding ﴿hours of the night﴾: "its beginning, its middle and its end."

* *

His saying: ﴿fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord﴾ means: in the state of his worship he is fearful and hopeful. Worship must include both of these, and fear should be predominant during the duration of life. For this reason He said: ﴿fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord﴾. So when one is at the point of death, hope should predominate over him, as the Imam 'Abd ibn Humayd related in his Musnad.

Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon a man who was dying, and he said to him: "How do you find yourself?" He said: "I hope and I fear." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "These two do not come together in the heart of a servant in such a situation except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives him what he hopes for and grants him security from what he fears."

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla," and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Sayyar ibn Hatim, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (strange). Some of them have related it from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) as mursal (with a missing companion)."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, from Ubaydah al-Numayri: Abu Khalaf 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa al-Khazzaz narrated to us: Yahya al-Bakka' narrated to us, that he heard Ibn 'Umar recite: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord?﴾ Ibn 'Umar said: "That is 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him."

Ibn 'Umar only said that because of the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman's abundance of prayer at night and his recitation, to the extent that he would sometimes recite the Qur'an in a single rak'ah, as Abu 'Ubaydah related from him, may Allah be pleased with him. The poet said:

"Sacrifice the grey-haired one, whose mark is prostration upon him, who divides the night with glorification and Qur'an."

Imam Ahmad said: al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' wrote to me: al-Haytham ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Waqid, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Tamim al-Dari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night, a night's qunut is recorded for him."

Al-Nasa'i also related it in "al-Yawm wa al-Layla," from Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub, from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf and al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', both from al-Haytham ibn Humayd, with the same chain.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ means: Are this one and the one before him, who set up rivals to Allah in order to lead others astray from His way, equal? ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾ means: only one who has intellect, which is reason, knows the difference between this and that.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His believing servants to persevere in His obedience and in their piety: ﴿Say: O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good﴾, meaning: for whoever does good deeds in this world there is good in their worldly life and in their Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah's earth is spacious﴾, Mujahid said: "Then emigrate within it, strive, and abandon the idols."

Shurayk narrated from Mansur, from 'Ata' concerning His saying: ﴿And Allah's earth is spacious﴾, that he said: "If you are called to disobedience, then flee. Then he recited: ﴿Was not Allah's earth spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?﴾ [An-Nisa, 97]."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without account﴾, al-Awza'i said: "It is not weighed for them nor measured; rather, it is given to them by handfuls."

Ibn Juraij said: "It has reached me that their reward for their deeds is never counted against them, but rather they are given increase beyond that."

As-Suddi said: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without account﴾ means: in Paradise.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾, meaning: I have only been commanded to devote worship sincerely to Allah alone, with no partner.

﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾. As-Suddi said: "Meaning, the first of his nation, may Allah bless him and grant him peace."

Allah the Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad, and you are the Messenger of Allah: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day﴾, and that is the Day of Resurrection. This is a conditional statement, and its meaning is an allusion to others by way of greater and more fitting reasoning: ﴿Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion. So worship what you will besides Him."﴾ This is also a threat and a disavowal of them. ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers"﴾, meaning: indeed the losers are those who lose completely, ﴿who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: they will be separated, and there will be no meeting for them ever, whether their families went to Paradise while they went to the Fire, or all of them were made to dwell in the Fire but without any gathering or joy for them. ﴿That is the manifest loss﴾, meaning: this is the clear, evident, plain loss.

Then He described their state in the Fire, saying: ﴿For them there will be canopies of Fire above them and canopies below them﴾, as He said: ﴿For them from Hell will be a bed, and over them coverings. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 41], and He said: ﴿The Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say, "Taste what you used to do."﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 55].

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 39, verse 17–18:

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, from his father: "﴿And those who avoid the Taghut (false deities), not worshipping them﴾ was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and Salman al-Farisi."

The sound view is that it encompasses them and others who avoided the worship of idols and turned in repentance to the worship of the Most Merciful. For these there is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.

Then He said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾, meaning: they understand it and act upon what is in it, like His saying, Exalted is He, to Musa when He gave him the Torah: ﴿Hold it firmly and command your people to take the best of it﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾, meaning: those who possess this attribute are the ones whom Allah has guided in this world and the Hereafter [[In the manuscript S: "wal-ukhra" (and the other)]], that is, the people of sound intellects and upright natural disposition.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 39, verse 17–18:

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, from his father: "﴿And those who avoid the Taghut (false deities), not worshipping them﴾ was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and Salman al-Farisi."

The sound view is that it encompasses them and others who avoided the worship of idols and turned in repentance to the worship of the Most Merciful. For these there is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.

Then He said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾, meaning: they understand it and act upon what is in it, like His saying, Exalted is He, to Musa when He gave him the Torah: ﴿Hold it firmly and command your people to take the best of it﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾, meaning: those who possess this attribute are the ones whom Allah has guided in this world and the Hereafter [[In the manuscript S: "wal-ukhra" (and the other)]], that is, the people of sound intellects and upright natural disposition.

Allah, the Exalted, says: "Then is one against whom the Word of punishment has been decreed [someone you can] rescue from the error and destruction he is in?" That is, no one can guide him after Allah, for "whomever Allah leaves to stray, there is no guide for him, and whomever He guides, there is no misleader for him."

Then He informs of His righteous servants that they have chambers in Paradise, which are lofty palaces: ﴿For them are chambers, one built above another﴾. That is, layer above layer, well-built, firmly constructed, adorned, and elevated.

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abbad ibn Yaʿqub al-Asadi related to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nuʿman ibn Saʿd, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are chambers whose outsides can be seen from their insides, and whose insides can be seen from their outsides." A Bedouin said: "For whom are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For those who speak kindly, feed the food, and pray at night while people are asleep."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq [[Zawaid ʿAbd Allah on the Musnad (1/155) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1984).]], and said: "Hasan gharib, and some scholars have spoken about him from the perspective of his memorization."

Imam Ahmad also said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, Maʿmar related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ibn Muʿanaq, or Abu Muʿanaq, from Abu Malik al-Ashʿari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a chamber [[In S and A: "ghurfah".]] whose outside can be seen from its inside, and whose inside can be seen from its outside. Allah has prepared it for those who feed the food, soften their speech, persist in fasting, and pray while people are asleep."

Ahmad alone narrated it from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muʿanaq al-Ashʿari, from Abu Malik, with this wording.

Imam Ahmad also said: Qutaybah ibn Saʿid related to us, Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, from Abu Hazim [[In T: "with its isnad."]], from Sahl ibn Saʿd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the people of Paradise will look at the chamber in Paradise just as you look at the star in the sky." He said: "I related that to al-Nuʿman ibn Abi Ayyash, and he said: I heard Abu Saʿid al-Khudri say: 'Just as you look at the bright star on the eastern or western horizon.'"

They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hazim [[Musnad (5/340), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6555), and Sahih Muslim no. (2830).]]. They also both narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Malik, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from ʿAta ibn Yasar, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6556) and Sahih Muslim no. (2831).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Fazarah related to us, Fulayh informed me, from Hilal ibn ʿAli, from ʿAta ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the people of Paradise will look at the people of the chambers in Paradise, just as you look at the bright star that is setting on the rising horizon, due to the difference in the ranks of the people of the degrees." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they the Prophets?" He said: "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul, and (also) people who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Suwayd [[In A: "Yazid".]], from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Fulayh, with it, and said: "Hasan sahih."

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Kamil [[In A: "and Abu ʿAmir".]] related to us, saying: Zuhayr related to us, Saʿd al-Taʾi related to us, Abu al-Mudallah, the mawla of the Mother of the Believers, related to us, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we see you, our hearts become tender, and we are among the people of the Hereafter. But when we part from you, the world delights us, and we become attached to women and children." He said: "If you were always in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake hands with you and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, Allah would bring a people who sin, so that He might forgive them." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us about Paradise, what is its construction?" He said: "A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is musk of the strongest fragrance, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its dust is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not despair, will live forever and will not die, his garments will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. Three whose supplication is not rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the oppressed, which is carried upon the clouds, the gates of the heavens are opened for it, and the Lord says: 'By My might, I will surely help you, even if after a while.'" [[Musnad (2/304).]]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated part of it from the hadith of Saʿd [[In A: "ʿAyd".]] Abu Mujahid al-Taʾi, who was trustworthy, from Abu al-Mudallah, who was trustworthy, with it [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3598) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1752). Al-Tirmidhi said: "This hadith is hasan," then pointed to the lengthy narration of Ahmad.]].

That is, no one can guide him after Allah, for "whomever Allah leaves to stray, there is no guide for him, and whomever He guides, there is no misleader for him."

Then He informs of His righteous servants that they have chambers in Paradise, which are lofty palaces: ﴿For them are chambers, one built above another﴾. That is, layer above layer, well-built, firmly constructed, adorned, and elevated.

Allah the Exalted informs that the origin of water in the earth is from the sky, as He said: ﴿And We sent down from the sky pure water﴾ [Al-Furqan: 48]. So when He sends down water from the sky, it is like what is in the earth. Then Allah the Exalted directs it through the parts of the earth as He wills, and makes it gush forth as springs, small and large, according to the need for them. For this reason He said: ﴿Then threaded it as springs in the earth﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim [In manuscript T: "narrated"], may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Abu Qutaybah Utbah ibn Yaqzan narrated to us, from Ikrimah [In manuscript T: "with his chain"], from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, then threads it as springs in the earth?﴾ He said: There is no water in the earth except that it descended from the sky, but veins in the earth alter it. That is His saying: ﴿Then threads it as springs in the earth﴾. Whoever is pleased that salt water become sweet, let him make it ascend (evaporate it).

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Amir al-Sha'bi: that every water in the earth has its origin in the sky.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said: Its origin is from snow. That is, the snow accumulates on the mountains and settles in their bases, and then the springs gush forth from their lower parts.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then He brings forth by it crops of varying colours﴾ means: then He brings forth, by the water descending from the sky and welling up from the earth, crops ﴿of varying colours﴾, that is, of varying forms, tastes, smells and benefits. ﴿Then it dries up﴾, that is, after its freshness and youth it grows old, ﴿so you see it turn yellow﴾, having been mixed with dryness. ﴿Then He makes it debris﴾, that is, then it returns dry and crumbles. ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾, that is, those who take heed from this and reflect that this world is just like this: it is green, fresh and beautiful, then it returns as an old, ugly woman; and the young man returns to being an old, decrepit, very weak man [who has been mixed with dryness]. After all that comes death. The happy one is the one whose condition after it is good. Allah the Exalted often strikes the example of the life of this world with what He sends down from the sky of water, by which He causes crops and fruits to grow, and then afterwards they become debris, as He said: ﴿And strike for them the example of the life of this world: it is like water that We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, then it becomes dry stalks which the winds scatter. And Allah is ever Capable of all things﴾ [Al-Kahf: 45].

* *

As in His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, not coming out of it?﴾ [Al-An'am: 122]. For this reason He said: ﴿So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾, that is, they do not soften at His remembrance, nor do they humble themselves, nor do they heed, nor do they understand. ﴿Those are in clear error﴾.

This is a praise from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His Book, the Great Quran, which was sent down to His Noble Messenger. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah has sent down the most beautiful statement, a Book consistent with itself and oft-repeated (mathani)﴾. Mujahid said: "It means the entire Quran is mutashabih (consistent with itself, its parts resembling one another) and mathani."

Qatadah said: "A verse resembles another verse, and a letter resembles another letter."

Al-Dahhak said: "Mathani means the repetition of statements so that they may understand from their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic."

Ikrimah and al-Hasan said: "Allah repeats the decrees within it." Al-Hasan added: "A surah contains a verse, and another surah contains a verse that resembles it."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Mathani means repeated. Musa, Salih, Hud and the prophets, upon them be peace, are repeated in the Quran in many places."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas: "Mathani: the Quran resembles some of itself, and some of it is repeated over other parts." (In A: "yuraddadu", i.e., "is repeated.")

Some scholars said: It is related from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah that the meaning of His words ﴿consistent with itself and oft-repeated﴾ is that the contexts of the Quran are sometimes about one single meaning, and this is mutashabih. And sometimes they mention a thing and its opposite, such as mentioning the believers and then the disbelievers, or the description of Paradise and then the description of Hell, and similar to this. This is from the mathani. As He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ (Al-Infitar 82:13-14), and His words ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ (Al-Mutaffifin 83:7), up to His saying ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun﴾ (Al-Mutaffifin 83:18), and ﴿This is a reminder. And indeed for the righteous is a good place of return﴾ (Sad 38:49), up to His saying ﴿This, and indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return﴾ (Sad 38:55), and similar contexts. All of this is from the mathani, that is, in two opposite meanings. But when the context is entirely about one meaning, with parts resembling one another, this is the mutashabih, and this is not the mutashabih mentioned in His words ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are decisive (muhkamat), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are mutashabihat﴾ (Ali 'Imran 3:7). That is another meaning.

* *

As for His words ﴿The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾: this describes the righteous, when they hear the speech of the Compeller, the Almighty, the Forgiving, because of what they understand from it of promise and threat, and of warning and intimidation. Their skins shiver out of fear and dread, ﴿then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, out of hope and expectation of His mercy and kindness. They differ from other disbelievers (fajir) in several respects:

The first: their hearing is the recitation of the verses, while the hearing of those others is the melodies of verses sung to tunes, from the voices of singing girls.

The second: when the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrate and weeping, with courtesy, fear, hope, love, understanding and knowledge, as He said: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely; those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them. Those are the believers in truth; for them are degrees with their Lord, and forgiveness and a noble provision﴾ (Al-Anfal 8:2-4). And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:73). That means: they are not, when hearing them, busy, heedless or inattentive; rather they listen attentively, understanding and perceiving their meanings. Therefore they act upon them, and they prostrate at them with insight, not out of ignorance or merely following others [i.e., they see others prostrating and so prostrate following them] . [[Addition from A.]]

The third: they observe courtesy when hearing them, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did when they heard the speech of Allah from the recitation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): their skins shivered, then their skins softened together with their hearts to the remembrance of Allah. They did not shout out or feign what was not in them. Rather they had, in that, a steadiness, calm, courtesy and fear that no one could match. Therefore they attained the highest prize in this world and the Hereafter.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar related to us, saying: Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, recited: ﴿The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾.

He said: "This describes the friends of Allah. Allah described them as having their skins shiver, their eyes weep, and their hearts become tranquil in the remembrance of Allah. He did not describe them as losing their minds or swooning. That belongs to the people of innovation, and it is from Satan."

Al-Suddi said: "﴿Then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: to the promise of Allah." And His words ﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills of His servants﴾ mean: this is the attribute of those whom Allah has guided. Whoever is contrary to that is among those whom Allah has misguided: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ (Al-Ra'd 13:33).

Allah the Exalted says: "Is one who will shield his face with his own face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is secure]?" And it will be said to him and to those like him among the wrongdoers, as a rebuke: "Taste what you used to earn." [Is he] like one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?! As Allah the Exalted said: "Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?" [al-Mulk 67:22]. And He said: "The Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces: 'Taste the touch of Saqar.'" [al-Qamar 54:48]. And He said: "Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?" [Fussilat 41:40]. In this verse He has mentioned only one of the two categories, leaving the other to be understood, like the saying of the poet [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (22/98).]]:

"I do not know, when I set out for a land, seeking good, which of the two will meet me..."

That is, good or evil.

* *

As for His saying: "Those before them denied, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive" [az-Zumar 39:25], it means the past generations who denied the messengers. Allah destroyed them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.

* *

As for His saying: "So Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world" [az-Zumar 39:26], that is, by the punishment and retribution He sent upon them, and by the believers being pleased with their suffering. So let those addressed take warning from this, for they have denied the most noble of the messengers and the seal of the prophets. The severe punishment that Allah has prepared for them in the Hereafter is greater than what befell them in this world. Therefore He said: "And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew" [az-Zumar 39:26].

al-Tirmidhi related it from the narration of Muhammad ibn 'Amr with it, and said: Hasan sahih.

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id related to us: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Abu 'Ushshanah, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first of the two disputants on the Day of Resurrection will be two neighbours." Ahmad alone related it.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa related to us: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us: Darraj related to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed, [even] two sheep will dispute when they butt each other." Ahmad alone related it.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Sahl ibn Bahr related to us, Hayyan ibn Aghlab related to us, my father related to us, Thabit related to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection the treacherous ruler will be brought, and his subjects will dispute with him and prevail over him, and it will be said to him: Block a corner of the corners of Hell."

Then he said: al-Aghlab ibn Tamim is not a hafiz.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, regarding ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾, that he said: the truthful will dispute with the liar, the oppressed with the oppressor, the guided with the misguided, and the weak with the arrogant.

The soul will say to the body: You did it. And the body will say to the soul: You commanded it, and you enticed it. Then Allah will send an angel to judge between them, and he will say to them: Your likeness is that of a man, paralysed but seeing, and the other blind, who entered a garden. The paralysed one said to the blind one: I see fruits here, but I cannot reach them. The blind one said to him: Mount me, and pick them. So he mounted him and picked them. Which of them is the transgressor? They will say: Both of them. The angel will say to them: You have both judged against yourselves. meaning: that the body is to the soul like a mount, and it is its rider.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn 'Awsajah related to us, Dirar related to us, Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i Mansur ibn Salamah related to us, al-Qummi – meaning Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah – related to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: This verse was revealed, and we did not know about what it was revealed: ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾. al-Nasa'i related it from Muhammad ibn 'Amir, from Mansur ibn Salamah, with it.

Abu al-'Aliyah said regarding His saying ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾: it means the People of the Qiblah.

Ibn Zayd said: it means the People of Islam and the People of Disbelief.

And He said: ﴿And these examples We present to the people, but none understands them except the knowledgeable﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 43].

* *

Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] made it so and sent it down thus, ﴿so that they may be mindful of Allah﴾, meaning: that they may beware of the threats within it, and act upon what it contains of promises [[In manuscripts T and A: "what" (lima) rather than "that" (ma); and "threat" (al-wa'id) rather than "promise".]].

Then He said: ﴿Allah presents an example: a man in whom are partners at variance with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man﴾, meaning: they dispute over that slave who is owned jointly among them, ﴿and a man wholly devoted to one man﴾, meaning: exclusively belonging to one man, whom no one else owns, ﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾, meaning: this and that are not equal. The Most High says, addressing the polytheists who fabricated lies against God, associated other gods with Him, claimed that the angels are God's daughters, and attributed offspring to God. Exalted is God far above what they say. Yet despite this, they denied the truth when it came to them through the tongues of God's messengers, may God's blessings [and peace] be upon them all. Therefore He said: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who lies against God and denies the truth when it comes to him?﴾ That is, no one is more unjust than this, because he combined both extremes of falsehood: he lied against God and denied the Messenger of God. They spoke falsehood and rejected the truth. Therefore He said, warning them: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾, meaning those who deny and reject.

Then He said: ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it﴾. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿the one who brings the truth﴾ is the Messenger. Al-Suddi said: it is Jibril (peace be upon him), and ﴿confirms it﴾ means Muhammad ﷺ.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And the one who brings the truth﴾, he said: whoever brings "There is no god but God", ﴿and confirms it﴾, meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas recited: "Those who brought the truth and confirmed it", meaning the prophets, and "they confirmed it", meaning the followers.

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym reported from Mujahid: ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it﴾, he said: the believing companions of the Qur'an will come on the Day of Resurrection and say: "This is what You gave us, and we acted upon what You commanded us."

This statement from Mujahid includes all believers, for the believer speaks the truth and acts upon it. The Messenger ﷺ is the most deserving of entry into this verse according to this interpretation, for he brought the truth, confirmed the messengers, and believed in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers, each of them believed in God, His angels, His books and His messengers.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him.﴾ That is, the polytheists frighten the Messenger and threaten him with their idols and gods which they worship besides Him, out of their ignorance and misguidance. Therefore Allah says: ﴿And whomever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide. And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Almighty, Owner of Retribution?﴾ That is, the Mighty whose protection cannot be violated, whoever takes refuge in His protection and seeks shelter at His door. He is the Mighty, than whom none is mightier, and none is more severe in retribution against those who disbelieve in Him, associate others with Him, and oppose His Messenger (ﷺ).

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book⦆ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿for mankind, in truth⦆, i.e., for all of creation, both mankind and jinn, so that you may warn them by it. ﴿Whoever is guided, it is for his own self⦆, i.e., the benefit of that returns only to himself. ﴿And whoever strays, only to its detriment does he stray⦆, i.e., the burden of that returns only upon himself. ﴿And you are not over them a guardian⦆, i.e., you are not entrusted with making them guided. ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things⦆ [Hud: 12]. ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the account⦆ [Ar-Ra'd: 40].

Then Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about His own noble Self that He is the One who disposes of existence as He wills, and that He takes the souls with the great death (al-wafat al-kubra), by sending the angels (al-hafadhah) who seize them from the bodies, and with the lesser death (al-wafat al-sughra) at sleep, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who takes you in death by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein until a specified term is fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do. And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail⦆ [Al-An'am: 60–61]. So He mentioned the two deaths: the lesser, then the greater. In this verse He mentioned the greater, then the lesser; hence He said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term⦆. In it is an indication that they (the souls) gather in the highest assembly (al-mala' al-a'la), as the marfu' hadith narrated by Ibn Mandah and others indicates.

In the Sahihayn of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you goes to his bed, let him shake it with the inside of his waist-wrap, for he does not know what has fallen onto it after him. Then let him say: 'In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in You I raise it. If You take my soul, then have mercy on it, and if You release it, then protect it with what You protect Your righteous servants'" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6320) and Sahih Muslim no. (2714)].

Some of the early scholars [may Allah have mercy on them] said: He seizes the spirits of the dead when they die, and the spirits of the living when they sleep, so they become acquainted with one another as much as Allah wills them to become acquainted. ﴿Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death⦆, namely those that have died, and releases the others until a specified term.

As-Suddi said: "until the remainder of their term." Ibn Abbas said: "He keeps the souls of the dead and releases the souls of the living, and He does not err." ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect⦆.

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book⦆ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿for mankind, in truth⦆, i.e., for all of creation, both mankind and jinn, so that you may warn them by it. ﴿Whoever is guided, it is for his own self⦆, i.e., the benefit of that returns only to himself. ﴿And whoever strays, only to its detriment does he stray⦆, i.e., the burden of that returns only upon himself. ﴿And you are not over them a guardian⦆, i.e., you are not entrusted with making them guided. ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things⦆ [Hud: 12]. ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the account⦆ [Ar-Ra'd: 40].

Then Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about His own noble Self that He is the One who disposes of existence as He wills, and that He takes the souls with the great death (al-wafat al-kubra), by sending the angels (al-hafadhah) who seize them from the bodies, and with the lesser death (al-wafat al-sughra) at sleep, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who takes you in death by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein until a specified term is fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do. And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail⦆ [Al-An'am: 60–61]. So He mentioned the two deaths: the lesser, then the greater. In this verse He mentioned the greater, then the lesser; hence He said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term⦆. In it is an indication that they (the souls) gather in the highest assembly (al-mala' al-a'la), as the marfu' hadith narrated by Ibn Mandah and others indicates.

In the Sahihayn of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you goes to his bed, let him shake it with the inside of his waist-wrap, for he does not know what has fallen onto it after him. Then let him say: 'In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in You I raise it. If You take my soul, then have mercy on it, and if You release it, then protect it with what You protect Your righteous servants'" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6320) and Sahih Muslim no. (2714)].

As-Suddi said: "until the remainder of their term." Ibn Abbas said: "He keeps the souls of the dead and releases the souls of the living, and He does not err." ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect⦆.

Allah, exalted is He, says, censuring the polytheists for taking intercessors besides Allah. These are the idols and the rivals (*andad*, equals set up with Allah), which they took of their own accord, without any proof or evidence to guide them to it. They own nothing of the affair. Moreover, they have no intellect with which to reason, no hearing with which to hear, and no sight with which to see. Rather, they are inanimate objects, far worse off than living creatures by a great deal.[[In manuscript S: "bi-kabir" (a variant reading).]]

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad (ﷺ), to these people who claim that what they have taken as intercessors for them with Allah will intercede: inform them that intercession does not benefit with Allah except for one whom He approves and permits. So all of it belongs to Him, ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255].

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, He is the one who disposes of all of that. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned.﴾ That is, on the Day of Resurrection, when He will judge among you with His justice and recompense each person according to his deeds.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, again censuring the polytheists: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned﴾, that is, when it is said, "There is no god but Allah," ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink in aversion.﴾ Mujahid said: ﴿shrink﴾ means "contract" (*inqabadat*).

Al-Suddi said: "they recoil with aversion." Qatadah said: "they disbelieve and become arrogant." Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam: "they become arrogant." This is like Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant﴾ [As-Saffat: 35], that is, they refused to follow it and submit to it. Thus their hearts do not accept good, and whoever does not accept good will accept evil. For this reason He said: ﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned﴾, that is, the idols and rivals, as Mujahid said, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾, that is, they are delighted and pleased.

Allah, the Exalted, says, after mentioning the reproach directed at the polytheists for their love of shirk and their aversion to tawhid:

﴿Say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed."﴾ That is: Call upon Allah alone, with no partner, the One who created the heavens and the earth and brought them into being (fataraha), i.e., made them without a precedent pattern. ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ means: the secret and the manifest. ﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ means: in their worldly affairs (dunyahum) [In manuscript A: "dinan lahum" (a religion for them)]. You will decide between them on their Day of Return, their resurrection, and their rising from their graves.

Muslim related in his Sahih: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, who said: I asked Aisha [may Allah be pleased with her] with what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to open his prayer when he rose for the night prayer. She said: When he rose for the night prayer, he would open his prayer with: "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in what has been disputed, for You guide whom You will to a straight path." [Sahih Muslim, no. (770).] Imam Ahmad also said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, and Suhayl ibn Abi Salih and Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym informed us, from Awn ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud [may Allah be pleased with him] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I bind myself to You in this world that I testify that there is no god but You alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger; for if You leave me to myself, You bring me near to evil and distance me from good, and I trust only in Your mercy, so grant me a covenant with You that You will fulfill for me on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not break the promise,' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say to His angels on the Day of Resurrection: 'My servant has made a covenant with Me, so fulfill it for him,' and Allah will admit him to Paradise."

Suhayl said: I informed al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman that Awn had reported such-and-such, and he said: "There is not a girl in our household but she recites this in her chamber." Imam Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (1/412); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/174): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Hayy ibn Abd Allah narrated to me, that Abu Abd al-Rahman told him, who said: Abd Allah ibn Amr brought out a sheet of paper for us and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to teach us to say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You are the Lord of everything and its God. I testify that there is no god but You, alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, and the angels testify. I seek refuge with You from Satan and his shirk, and I seek refuge with You from committing a sin against myself or dragging it upon a Muslim."

Abu Abd al-Rahman said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to teach Abd Allah ibn Amr to say this when he wanted to sleep. Imam Ahmad alone narrated it as well. [Musnad (2/171).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Alhani, from Abu Rashid al-Hubrani, who said: I came to Abd Allah ibn Amr and said to him: "Tell us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He threw before me a sheet and said: "This is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote for me." I looked into it and there was in it that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq ["al-Siddiq radiya Allah anhu" in manuscript T] said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me what to say when I enter the morning and when I enter the evening." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu Bakr, say: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, there is no god but You, Lord and Sovereign of everything. I seek refuge with You from the evil of my soul, and the evil of Satan and his shirk, or that I commit evil against myself, or drag it upon a Muslim.'"

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Arafah, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, with the same chain, and said: "Hasan gharib from this route." [Musnad (2/196); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3529).]

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded me to say when I enter the morning and when I enter the evening, and when I take my bed at night: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth,'" up to its end. [Musnad (1/14).]

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him, reporting about man: when he is in adversity he humbles himself before Allah, turns to Him and calls upon Him; but when He bestows upon him a blessing from Himself, he transgresses and becomes arrogant, and says: ﴿I have only been given it because of knowledge﴾, meaning: because of what Allah knows of my deservingness of it; and were it not that I am especially favored with Allah, He would not have bestowed this upon me!

Qatadah said: ﴿on knowledge I have﴾ means: on good that I have.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Rather, it is a trial﴾, meaning: the matter is not as they claim. Rather, We bestowed this blessing upon him so that We may test him regarding what We have bestowed upon him: will he obey or disobey? While We already have prior knowledge of that. So it is a trial, that is, a test. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, and for this reason they say what they say and claim what they claim.

﴿Those before them said it already﴾, meaning: this statement was made, and this claim was asserted, and this pretension was advanced by many of the nations who passed before them. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾, meaning: their saying did not hold true, and their accumulation and what they used to earn did not protect them.

﴿So the evils of what they earned befell them; and those who wronged among these people, the evils of what they earned will befall them too, and they cannot escape﴾, meaning: among those addressed. ﴿The evils of what they earned will befall them﴾, meaning: just as it befell those. ﴿And they cannot escape﴾ — as Allah, the Exalted, reported concerning Qarun, that his people said to him: ﴿Do not exult; indeed Allah does not love the exultant. But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of this world. And do good as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land; indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾ He said: ﴿I have only been given it because of knowledge I have.﴾ Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation? And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins﴾ [al-Qasas 28:76–78]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they said: We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished﴾ [Saba' 34:35].
