Then He called to the repentance of one who is greater in his statement than these, one who said: ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24], and said: ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ [al-Qasas: 38]. Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with them both] [[added from T.]] said: Whoever despairs the servants of Allah of repentance after this has denied the Book of Allah, but the servant cannot repent until Allah turns to him in repentance.

Al-Tabarani related from the route of al-Sha'bi, from Shu'ayr ibn Shakl, that he said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: The greatest verse in the Book of Allah is: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. And the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an for good and evil is: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and beneficence﴾ [al-Nahl: 90]. And the verse in the Qur'an with the most relief is in Surat al-Ghuraf: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾. And the verse in the Book of Allah with the most severe [[in T, S: "with the most explicit (tafwid)"]] is: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq: 2-3]. Masruq said to him: "You have spoken truly."

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu al-Kanud, who said: 'Abd Allah [that is, Ibn Mas'ud] passed by a storyteller who was admonishing people, and he said: "O admonisher, why do you make people despair?" Then he recited: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Mention of hadiths in which despair is negated:

Imam Ahmad said: Suraij ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu 'Ubaydah 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, Akhshan al-Sadusi narrated to me, who said: I entered upon Anas ibn Malik and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you were to commit errors until your sins filled what is between the heaven and the earth, then you sought forgiveness from Allah, He would forgive you. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you did not commit errors, Allah would bring a people who commit errors, then they would seek forgiveness from Allah, and He would forgive them." Ahmad alone narrated it [[al-Musnad (3/238)]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Layth narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Qays – the storyteller of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz – narrated to me, from Abu Sirmah, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said when death was present to him: "I had concealed from you something I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: 'Were it not that you sin, Allah would create a people who sin, and He would forgive them.'"

Thus did Imam Ahmad relate it, and Muslim in his Sahih, and al-Tirmidhi, all of them, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (5/414), Sahih Muslim no. (2748), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3539)]]. Muslim also related it by another route with the same wording, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Sirmah – who was an Ansari Companion – from Abu Ayyub, with the same wording [[Sahih Muslim no. (2748)]].

Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Harrani narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Amr ibn Malik al-Nukri narrated to us, saying: I heard my father narrate from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas [[in A: "Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both"]], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The expiation of sin is regret," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you did not commit sins, Allah would bring a people who commit sins, and He would forgive them." Ahmad alone narrated it [[al-Musnad (1/289)]].

'Abd Allah, the son of Imam Ahmad, said: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad al-Narsi narrated to me, Dawud ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Abu 'Abd Allah Maslamah al-Razi narrated to us, from Abu 'Amr al-Bajali, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sufyan al-Thaqafi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, from his father, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah loves the servant who is tested and repents often." They did not narrate it through this route [[Zawa'id 'Abd Allah on the Musnad (1/80)]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 39, verses 53–59 (part 2 of 2):

And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit and Humayd informed us, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Iblis (may the curses of Allah be upon him) said: "O Lord, You expelled me from the Garden because of Adam, and I cannot overcome him except by Your authority." He said: "You are given power." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "No child will be born to him except that a child like it will be born to you." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "I will make their chests dwellings for you, and you will flow through them as the blood flows." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "Call upon them with your horsemen and your footmen, share with them in wealth and children, and promise them; and Satan does not promise them except as deception."

Then Adam (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, You have given him power over me, and I cannot protect myself from him except by You." He said: "No child will be born to you except that I will appoint for him someone to guard him from evil companions." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "The good deed is multiplied tenfold, or I increase it further, and the bad deed is one, or I erase it." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "The door of repentance is open as long as the soul is in the body." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

And Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Nafi' said, from Abdullah ibn Umayr, from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), in his hadith, he said: "We used to say that Allah will not accept from one who has been tested: neither exchange nor ransom nor repentance, [those] who knew Allah and then returned to disbelief because of a trial that befell them." He said: "And they used to say that about themselves." He said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, Allah revealed concerning them and concerning what we said and what they said about themselves: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped. And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾."

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "So I wrote it with my own hand on a sheet, and sent it to Hisham ibn al-As." He said: Hisham said: "When it reached me, I began reading it at Dhu Tuwa, climbing up with it and raising my voice, and I did not understand it, until I said: 'O Allah, grant me understanding of it.'" He said: "Then Allah cast into my heart that it was only revealed concerning us, and concerning what we used to say about ourselves, and what was said about us. So I returned to my camel, sat upon it, and caught up with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah."

Then Allah, glorified is He and exalted, urged His servants to hasten to repentance, saying: ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him﴾, meaning: return to Allah and surrender to Him. ﴿before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped﴾, meaning: hasten to repentance and righteous deeds before the coming of vengeance.

﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, which is the Great Qur'an. ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾, meaning: from where you do not know and do not realize.

Then He said: ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Alas, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah"﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, the criminal who neglected repentance and turning back will regret, and will wish that he had been among the good, the sincere, and the obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I was among those who mocked﴾, meaning: my deeds in the world were only the deeds of one who mocks and ridicules, who was not certain and did not affirm the truth.

﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous." Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another chance, that I might be among the doers of good."﴾ Meaning: they wish that they could be returned to the abode so that they might do good deeds.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: Allah, glorified is He, informed of what the servants would say before they said it, and of their deeds before they did them, and said: ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ (Fatir: 14), ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Alas, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah, and indeed I was among those who mocked. Or lest it say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.' Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, 'If only I had another chance, that I might be among the doers of good.'"﴾ So Allah the Exalted informed that if they were returned, they would not be able to attain guidance. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ (al-An'am: 28).

The Imam Ahmad has related: Aswad narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every person of the Fire will see his seat in Paradise, and he will say, 'If only Allah had guided me!' so that will be a regret for him." He said: "And every person of Paradise will see his seat in the Fire, and he will say, 'Were it not that Allah guided me!' " He said: "So that will be a cause for gratitude for him."

An-Nasa'i also related it through the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (2/512).]

When the people of crimes wished to return to the world, and regretted not having affirmed the signs of Allah and followed His messengers, Allah, glorified is He and exalted, said: ﴿Yes! My signs had come to you, but you denied them, and you were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers﴾ [The word "qul" (say) in one manuscript is an error.] That is: My signs had come to you, O servant who regrets what he did, in the worldly abode, and My proofs were established against you, but you denied them and were arrogant toward following them, and you were among the disbelievers in them, the deniers of them.

This noble verse is a call to all the sinners, among the disbelievers and others, to repentance and turning back to Allah, and an announcement that Allah forgives all sins for whoever repents from them and turns away from them, however great they are, however many they become, and even if they are like the foam of the sea. It is not valid to interpret this verse [[added from A.]] as referring to anyone other than one who repents [[in T: "repentance"]], because shirk is not forgiven for one who does not repent from it.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them. Ya'la said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed him, from Ibn 'Abbas [[in T: "Al-Bukhari narrated with his chain from Ibn 'Abbas"]] [may Allah be pleased with them both] [[added from A.]], that some people from among the polytheists had killed many people and committed much fornication. They came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good, if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done." Then there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], and there was revealed [[added from T, S.]]: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾.

Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related it in the same way, from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Ya'la ibn Muslim al-Makki, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4810), Sahih Muslim no. (122), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (7274), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/86)]].

The intended meaning of the first verse is His saying: ﴿except for those who repent and believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], and the verse.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Abu Qabil narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muri [[in A: "al-Sari"]] say: I heard Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I would not love to have the world and whatever is in it in exchange for this verse: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾" up to the end of the verse. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the one who associates partners [with Allah]?" The Prophet (ﷺ) was silent, then said: "Unquestionably, and the one who associates partners [with Allah]," three times. Ahmad alone narrated it [[al-Musnad (5/275)]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Suraij [[in A: "Shurayh"]] ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, Rawh ibn Qays narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Jabir al-Huddani, from Makhul, from 'Amr ibn 'Abasa [[in T, I: "'Anbasa"]], who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ), an elderly man leaning on his staff, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have had acts of treachery and acts of immorality, will I be forgiven?" He said: "Do you not testify that there is no god but Allah?" He said: "Yes, and I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Your acts of treachery and immorality have been forgiven." Ahmad alone narrated it [[al-Musnad (4/385)]].

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Shahr ibn Hawshab [[in T: "And he also related"]], from Asma' bint Yazid [[in A: "Yazid, may Allah be pleased with her"]], who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite: ﴿Indeed, it is an unrighteous deed﴾ [Hud: 46], and I heard him say: "﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾" and he did not mind [the length], "﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi related it from the hadith of Thabit, with the same chain [[al-Musnad (6/454), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3982), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3237)]].

All these hadiths indicate that the intended meaning is that He forgives all of that together with repentance, and that no servant should despair of the mercy of Allah, even if his sins are great and many; for the door of repentance and mercy is wide. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 104]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa': 110]. And the Exalted said concerning the hypocrites: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper, except those who repent﴾ [al-Nisa': 145-146]. And He said: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the third of three," while there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 73]. Then He said: ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 74]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women and then have not repented﴾ [al-Buruj: 10].

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Look at this generosity and bounty! They killed His allies while He calls them to repentance and forgiveness!

The verses on this subject are very numerous.

In the two Sahihs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), is the hadith of the man [[in T: "that a man"]] who killed ninety-nine souls. Then he regretted and asked a worshipper from among the worshippers of the Children of Israel: "Is there repentance for me?" He said: "No." So he killed him and completed a hundred with him. Then he asked a scholar from among their scholars: "Is there repentance for me?" He said: "Who can come between you and repentance?" Then he ordered him to go to a village in which Allah is worshipped. He set out towards it, but death overtook him along the way. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. Allah commanded that they measure the distance between the two lands, and whichever of them he was nearer to, he belongs to it. They found him nearer by a span to the land to which he had migrated, so the angels of mercy seized him. It is mentioned that he leaned his chest forward at the time of death, that Allah commanded the good land to draw near, and commanded that other land to move away [[al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (3470), Muslim no. (2766)]]. This is the meaning of the hadith, and we have written it in another place in its full wording.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning His saying: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins"﴾ up to the end of the verse, he said: Allah has called to His forgiveness whoever claimed that the Messiah is Allah, and whoever claimed that the Messiah is the son of Allah, and whoever claimed that 'Uzair [[in T: "al-'Uzair"]] is the son of Allah, and whoever claimed that Allah is poor, and whoever claimed that the hand of Allah is chained, and whoever claimed that Allah is the third of three. Al-Tabarani related from the route of al-Sha'bi, from Shu'ayr ibn Shakl, that he said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: The greatest verse in the Book of Allah is: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. And the verse in the Qur'an with the most relief is in Surat al-Ghuraf: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾. And the verse in the Book of Allah with the most severe [[in T, S: "with the most explicit (tafwid)"]] is: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq: 2-3]. Masruq said to him: "You have spoken truly."

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu al-Kanud, who said: 'Abd Allah [that is, Ibn Mas'ud] passed by a storyteller who was admonishing people, and he said: "O admonisher, why do you make people despair?" Then he recited: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I was among those who mocked﴾, meaning: my deeds in the world were only the deeds of one who mocks and ridicules, who was not certain and did not affirm the truth.

﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous." Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another chance, that I might be among the doers of good."﴾ Meaning: they wish that they could be returned to the abode so that they might do good deeds.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: Allah, glorified is He, informed of what the servants would say before they said it, and of their deeds before they did them, and said: ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ (Fatir: 14), ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Alas, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah, and indeed I was among those who mocked. Or lest it say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.' Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, 'If only I had another chance, that I might be among the doers of good.'"﴾ So Allah the Exalted informed that if they were returned, they would not be able to attain guidance. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ (al-An'am: 28).

The Imam Ahmad has related: Aswad narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every person of the Fire will see his seat in Paradise, and he will say, 'If only Allah had guided me!' so that will be a regret for him." He said: "And every person of Paradise will see his seat in the Fire, and he will say, 'Were it not that Allah guided me!' " He said: "So that will be a cause for gratitude for him."

An-Nasa'i also related it through the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (2/512).]

When the people of crimes wished to return to the world, and regretted not having affirmed the signs of Allah and followed His messengers, Allah, glorified is He and exalted, said: ﴿Yes! My signs had come to you, but you denied them, and you were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers﴾ [The word "qul" (say) in one manuscript is an error.] That is: My signs had come to you, O servant who regrets what he did, in the worldly abode, and My proofs were established against you, but you denied them and were arrogant toward following them, and you were among the disbelievers in them, the deniers of them.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, concerning the Day of Resurrection, that on it some faces will turn black and some faces will turn white: the faces of the people of division and disagreement (ahl al-furqah wa'l-ikhtilaf) will turn black, and the faces of the people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (ahl al-sunnah wa'l-jama'ah) will turn white. Here Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah, their faces blackened﴾, meaning, in their claim that He has a partner and a son, ﴿their faces blackened﴾, meaning, by their lying and their fabrication.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾, meaning: Is Hell not sufficient for them as a prison and a refuge, in which is the abode of disgrace and humiliation for them, because of their arrogance, their tyranny, and their refusal to submit to the truth?

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubaid Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us; my paternal uncle narrated to us; Isa ibn Abi Isa al-Khayyat narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the likeness of ants in the forms of men; everything will overwhelm them of lowliness, until they enter a prison of Fire in a valley called Bulas, from the fire of al-Anyar, and they will be given to drink the pus of the people of the Fire and the sweat of the people of Khabal." [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (2/178), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 2492, by way of Muhammad ibn Ajlan from Amr ibn Shu'ayb in similar wording. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will save those who feared Him by their achievement﴾, meaning: by what had preceded for them of happiness and success with Allah; ﴿evil will not touch them﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection; ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, meaning: the greatest terror will not grieve them. Rather, they will be secure from every fright, kept far from every evil, and hoping for every good.

Rather, they will be secure from every fright, kept far from every evil, and hoping for every good.

He, the Exalted, informs that He is the Creator of all things, their Lord, their Sovereign, and the One who disposes of them. All of them are under His management, His dominion and His protection.

His saying: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.﴾ Mujahid said: "al-maqalid are al-mafatih (the keys)," in Persian. Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said the same.

al-Suddi said: "﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ means the treasuries of the heavens and the earth."

The meaning according to both views is that the reins of affairs are in His hand. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is Powerful over everything. Therefore He said: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., His proofs and evidences, ﴿they are the losers.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a very strange hadith, and its authenticity is questionable. Nevertheless, we mention it as he related it. He said:

Yazid [[In manuscript A: "Zayd".]] ibn Sinan al-Basri narrated to us in Egypt, Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, al-Aghlab ibn Tamim narrated to us, from Mukhallad ibn Hudhayl al-'Abdi, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Madani, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the explanation of: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.﴾ He said: "No one has asked me about it before you, O 'Uthman." He said: "Its explanation is: There is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and there is no power except with Allah; the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward; in His hand is all good; He gives life and causes death, and He is Powerful over everything. Whoever says them, O 'Uthman, ten times in the morning, will be given six qualities. As for the first: he will be guarded from Iblis and his soldiers. As for the second: he will be given a qintar (a great measure) of reward. As for the third: a degree will be raised for him in Paradise. As for the fourth: he will marry among the houris. As for the fifth: twelve angels will attend him. As for the sixth: he will be given the reward of one who recited the Qur'an, the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. And besides this, O 'Uthman, he will have the reward of one who performed Hajj and whose Hajj was accepted, and who performed 'Umrah and whose 'Umrah was accepted. If he dies that same day, he will be sealed with the seal of the martyrs."

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Hammad, with the same wording. [[Ibn al-Sunni narrated it in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla, no. 73, through Abu 'an Shuja' ibn Makhlad, from Yahya ibn Hammad, with it. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/115): "Abu Ya'la narrated it in al-Kabir, and in its chain is al-Aghlab ibn Tamim, who is weak."]] It is gharib (singular, i.e., narrated through a single chain), and it contains severe irregularity (nakarah). And Allah knows best.

And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers.﴾

This is like His saying: ﴿And if they had associated others with Allah, what they used to do would have been nullified for them.﴾ [al-An'am: 88]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: If they had measured Him with His true measure, they would not have denied Him.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ refers to the disbelievers who did not believe in Allah's power over them. Whoever believes that Allah is Capable of everything has measured Allah with His true measure, and whoever does not believe in that has not measured Allah with His true measure.

Many hadiths have been related concerning this noble verse, and the method regarding them and similar texts is the way of the early generations (al-Salaf), which is to let them pass as they came, without asking how (takyif) and without distortion (tahrif).

Al-Bukhari said: Regarding His saying ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾: Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Ubaidah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A rabbi (habr) from the rabbis came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, we find that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, places the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and all the creation on one finger, and then says: I am the King." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molar teeth showed, confirming the rabbi's words. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾ to the end of the verse. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4811]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places in his Sahih, and Imam Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the Tafsir sections of their Sunan, all from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ubaidah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, with similar wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, shall I tell you that Allah carries the creatures on one finger, the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, and the moist earth on one finger?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molar teeth showed. He said: And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ to the end of the verse.

Thus it was narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i, through several chains, from al-A'mash with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Ata, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting and said: "How do you say, O Abu al-Qasim: On the Day when Allah places the heaven on this [and he pointed with his index finger], and the earth on this, and the mountains on this, and all the creation on this" — all of this while pointing with his finger. He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in his Tafsir from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Kudaynah Yahya ibn al-Muhallab, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, with the same wording, and said: "Hasan sahih gharib; we do not know it except from this route."

Then al-Bukhari said: Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah grasps the earth and folds the heaven with His right hand, then says: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it by this route. Muslim narrated it by another route. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4812; Sahih Muslim, no. 2787, from the route of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah.]

Al-Bukhari also said in another place: Muqaddam ibn Muhammad narrated to us, my uncle al-Qasim ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Allah will grasp the earths on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, and the heavens will be in His right hand, then He says: I am the King."

He alone narrated it by this route too. Muslim narrated it by another route. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4812; Sahih Muslim, no. 2788, from the route of Salim ibn Abd Allah, from Abd Allah ibn Umar.] Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route with wording more detailed and longer than this context, saying:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah informed us, from Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse one day on the pulpit: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was doing this with his hand, moving it, turning it forward and back: "The Lord glorifies Himself: I am the Compeller, I am the Proud, I am the King, I am the Mighty, I am the Generous." The pulpit shook beneath the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we said: "It will certainly fall with him."

Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim (Muslim added: and Ya'qub ibn Abd al-Rahman), both from Abu Hazim, from Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam, from Ibn Umar, similarly.

The wording of Muslim, from Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam in this hadith, is: that he looked at Abd Allah ibn Umar, how he imitates the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Allah takes His heavens and His earths in His hand and says: "I am the King," and He closes His fingers and opens them: "I am the King," until I looked at the pulpit moving from its lowest part, so much so that I said: "Will it fall down with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?"

Al-Bazzar said: Sulayman ibn Sayf narrated to us, Abu Ali al-Hanafi narrated to us, Abbad al-Minqari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) narrated to us, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse on the pulpit: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ until he reached: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾, and the pulpit did so, it came and went three times.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Ubayd ibn Umayr, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, and said: "Sahih."

Al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mu'awiyah al-Utbi narrated to us, Hayyan ibn Nafi' ibn Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Salim al-Qaddah narrated to us, from Ma'mar ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Khunays, from Abu Shaybah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a group of his companions: "I will recite to you verses from the end of Surat al-Zumar; whoever among you weeps, Paradise is due to him." He recited from His saying: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ to the end of the surah. Some of them wept and some did not. Those who did not weep said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have striven to weep but have not wept." He said: "I will recite it to you again; whoever does not weep, let him feign weeping." This is a very strange hadith. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' that Bakr ibn Khunays is matruk (abandoned).]

Stranger than it is what he also narrated in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Hashim ibn Murthid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to me, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: There are three qualities I have hidden from My servants; if a man saw them he would never do evil again: if I uncovered My veil and he saw Me, so that he would be certain, and know how I act toward My creation when I come to them; and I folded the heavens with My hand, then folded the earth and the earths, then said: I am the King, who has kingship besides Me? Then I would show them Paradise and what I have prepared for them in it of every good, so that they would be certain of it; and I would show them Hellfire and what I have prepared for them in it of every evil, so that they would be certain of it. But I deliberately concealed that from them so that I might know how they would act, and I have made it clear to them." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir; in its isnad is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak and did not hear from his father.]

This chain is close in strength, and it is a version through which many hadiths are transmitted. And Allah knows best.

He, exalted is He, informs us about the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the great signs and mighty convulsions that will occur in it. His saying: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾. This is the second blast, the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-sa'q), by which the living among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will die, except whom Allah wills, as is explicitly stated and explained in the well-known hadith of the Trumpet. Then He takes the souls of the rest, until the last to die is the Angel of Death. The Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-Hayy al-Qayyum), who was first, and who is the Everlasting last, remains alone in eternity and permanence. He will say: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ [Ghafir 40:16] three times. Then He answers Himself: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾, meaning: He who is One and has subdued everything and decreed annihilation upon everything. Then He will bring back to life, first of all, Israfil, and command him to blow the Trumpet again, the second time, which is the third blast, the blast of resurrection. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾, meaning: they will be alive after they had been bones and crumbled remains, and they will become living, looking at the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It will be but a single shout, and behold, they will be upon the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:13-14]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Day He calls you, and you will answer with His praise, and you will think that you tarried only a little﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you will come forth﴾ [al-Rum 30:25].

Imam Ahmad said: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who narrated to us Shu'bah, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud say: I heard a man say to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr: "You say that the Hour will come at such and such time?" He said: "I had intended not to narrate anything to you. I only said: 'You will see a great matter after a little while.'" Then 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Dajjal will emerge among my community and remain among them for forty — I do not know whether forty days, forty years, forty months or forty nights — then Allah will send 'Isa ibn Maryam, who resembles 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. He will appear and Allah will destroy him. Then the people will remain after him for seven years with no enmity between any two. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of al-Sham, and no one who has in his heart even an atom's weight of faith will be left, except that it will take him, so that if one of them were in the core of a mountain, it would enter upon him." He said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "And the wicked of the people will remain, light as birds and with the minds of beasts, not recognising any good nor denouncing any evil." He said: "Then Satan will appear to them and say: 'Will you not answer?' He will command them to worship idols, and they will worship them, while in that state their provisions will be abundant and their lives pleasant. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one who hears it will fail to lend it his ear, and the first to hear it will be a man who is repairing his pool, and he will swoon, and then no one will remain who does not swoon. Then Allah will send — or He will cause to descend — rain like a dew — or a shade, Nu'man was uncertain — and from it the bodies of the people will grow. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said: 'O people, come to your Lord!' ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat 37:24]." He said: "Then it will be said: 'Bring out the company of the Fire.'" He said: "It will be said: 'How many?' It will be said: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.' On that day the children will be raised gray-haired, and on that day a shin will be uncovered."

Muslim alone included it in his Sahih.

Al-Bukhari said: 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Salih say: I heard Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Between the two blasts is forty." They said: "O Abu Hurayrah, forty days?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse." "And everything of the human will decay except the coccyx bone, from which the creation will be reassembled."

Abu Ya'la said: Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "I asked Jibril, peace be upon him, about this verse: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾. Who are those whom Allah did not will to swoon?" He said: "They are the martyrs, hanging their swords around His Throne. The angels of the Day of Resurrection will meet them on the way to the place of gathering with camels of ruby whose reins are softer than silk, whose strides reach as far as the eye of men can see. They will walk in Paradise and say, when the outing lengthens: 'Come, let us go to our Lord, exalted and majestic, that we may see how He judges among His creation.' My God will smile upon them, and whenever He smiles upon a servant in a station, there will be no reckoning for him."

All its narrators are trustworthy except the teacher of Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, for he is not known, and Allah knows best. [Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak from the path of Abu Usamah, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, in similar wording, and said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]

Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said: 'O people, come to your Lord!' ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat 37:24]." He said: "Then it will be said: 'Bring out the company of the Fire.'" He said: "It will be said: 'How many?' It will be said: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.' On that day the children will be raised gray-haired, and on that day a shin will be uncovered."

Muslim alone included it in his Sahih.

Al-Bukhari said: 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Salih say: I heard Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Between the two blasts is forty." They said: "O Abu Hurayrah, forty days?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse." "And everything of the human will decay except the coccyx bone, from which the creation will be reassembled."

Abu Ya'la said: Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "I asked Jibril, peace be upon him, about this verse: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾. Who are those whom Allah did not will to swoon?" He said: "They are the martyrs, hanging their swords around His Throne. The angels of the Day of Resurrection will meet them on the way to the place of gathering with camels of ruby whose reins are softer than silk, whose strides reach as far as the eye of men can see. They will walk in Paradise and say, when the outing lengthens: 'Come, let us go to our Lord, exalted and majestic, that we may see how He judges among His creation.' My God will smile upon them, and whenever He smiles upon a servant in a station, there will be no reckoning for him."

All its narrators are trustworthy except the teacher of Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, for he is not known, and Allah knows best. [Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak from the path of Abu Usamah, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, in similar wording, and said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾, meaning: it will be illuminated on the Day of Resurrection when the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, manifests Himself to the creatures for the judgment to be decided. ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾: Qatadah said: the Book of deeds. ﴿And the prophets will be brought﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: they will testify against their nations that they conveyed to them the messages of Allah. ﴿And the witnesses﴾: meaning the witnesses from among the angels who record the deeds of the servants, good and evil. ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least; and even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, and We suffice as Reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He will multiply it and give from Himself a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:40]. And for this reason He said: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, meaning: of good or evil. ﴿And He is most knowing of what they do﴾.

He, may He be exalted, informs about the state of the wretched disbelievers, how they are driven to the Fire. They are driven with harsh force, with rebuke, threat, and warning, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ [al-Tur 52:13], meaning they will be shoved into it with force. This is while they are thirsty and parched, as He said in another verse: ﴿The Day We gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd﴾ [Maryam 19:85-86]. In that state they are deaf, mute, and blind. Some of them walk on their faces, ﴿and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾ [al-Isra 17:97].

* *

His saying: ﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾ means: as soon as they arrive at it, its gates are swiftly opened for them, so that punishment may be hastened upon them. Then its keepers, the Zabaniyah (the angels of punishment), who are harsh in character and mighty in strength, say to them, in reproach, rebuke, and humiliation: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves?﴾ meaning from your own kind, with whom you are able to converse and from whom you can take knowledge. ﴿Reciting to you the verses of your Lord﴾ meaning they established against you the proofs and evidences for the truth of what they called you to. ﴿And warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ meaning they cautioned you about the evil of this Day? The disbelievers will say to them: ﴿Yes (came they)﴾, meaning: indeed they came to us, warned us, and established against us the proofs and evidences. ﴿But the word of punishment has become due upon the disbelievers.﴾

Meaning: rather, we denied them and opposed them, because of the wretchedness that had preceded for us, which we deserved, since we turned away from the truth toward falsehood. As He, may He be exalted, said, informing about them in another verse: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?" They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.'" And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the blaze."﴾ [al-Mulk 67:8-10], meaning they turned their blame back upon themselves with remorse. ﴿So they will acknowledge their sin. So away with the companions of the blaze!﴾ [al-Mulk 67:11], meaning: distance and loss for them.

* *

His saying here: ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ meaning: everyone who sees them and knows their state bears witness against them that they deserve the punishment. For this reason He did not attribute this saying to a specific speaker, but left it unattributed, to indicate that the whole existence bears witness against them that they deserve what they are in, by the judgment of the Just, the All-Aware upon them. Therefore He, may He be majestic and exalted, said: ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ meaning: remaining in it, with no exit for you from it and no release for you from it. ﴿So wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾ meaning: wretched is your destination and wretched is your resting place, because of your arrogance in the world and your refusal to follow the truth. It is He who brought you to what you are in, so the state is wretched and the outcome is wretched.

They are driven with harsh force, with rebuke, threat, and warning, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ [al-Tur 52:13], meaning they will be shoved into it with force. Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾ [al-Isra 17:97].
