His saying here: ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ meaning: everyone who sees them and knows their state bears witness against them that they deserve the punishment. For this reason He did not attribute this saying to a specific speaker, but left it unattributed, to indicate that the whole existence bears witness against them that they deserve what they are in, by the judgment of the Just, the All-Aware upon them. Therefore He, may He be majestic and exalted, said: ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ meaning: remaining in it, with no exit for you from it and no release for you from it. ﴿So wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾ meaning: wretched is your destination and wretched is your resting place, because of your arrogance in the world and your refusal to follow the truth. It is He who brought you to what you are in, so the state is wretched and the outcome is wretched.

This is a report about the state of the righteous believers when they are driven to Paradise in groups, mounted on noble she-camels. ﴿Zumaran﴾ means groups following one after another: first the closest ones (al-Muqarrabun), then the righteous (al-Abrar), then those who come after them. Each group goes with those similar to them: the prophets with the prophets, the truthful (al-Siddiqun) with their peers, the martyrs with their like, and the scholars with their equals. Every category goes with its own kind, and each group suits the others.

﴿Hatta idha ja'uha﴾ means that when they reach the gates of Paradise, after crossing the Sirat, they are held back on a bridge between Paradise and Hellfire. Wrongs that existed between them in the world are settled for them. When they have been purified and cleansed, they are given permission to enter Paradise. A hadith about the Trumpet (hadith al-Suwar) reports that when the believers reach the gates of Paradise, they consult among themselves about who should ask permission for them to enter. They go to Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, then Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, just as they did in the places of standing (al-'Arasat) when they asked for intercession with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He come to judge, so that the nobility of Muhammad (ﷺ) over all mankind might be made manifest in all these situations.

It is firmly established in Sahih Muslim, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the first intercessor in Paradise." In another wording in Muslim: "And I am the first to knock on the door of Paradise."

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us, Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will come to the gate of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection and ask for it to be opened. The gatekeeper will say: 'Who are you?' I will say: 'Muhammad.' He will say: 'It was commanded to me that I must not open it for anyone before you.'"

Muslim also narrated it from Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb, both from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Sulayman, who is Ibn al-Mughira al-Qaysi, from Thabit, from Anas, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first group to enter Paradise will have faces like the moon on the night of the full moon. They will not spit in it, nor blow their noses in it, nor defecate in it. Their vessels and combs will be of gold and silver, their censers will be of aloes wood, their sweat will be musk, and each of them will have two wives, through whose flesh the marrow of their shins can be seen because of their beauty. There will be no disagreement among them and no hatred; their hearts will be as one heart, and they will glorify Allah morning and evening."

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Muqatil, from Ibn al-Mubarak. Muslim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafi', from 'Abd al-Razzaq, both from Ma'mar with its chain, in similar wording. Likewise, Abu al-Zinad narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Khaythama narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those who follow them will be in the light of the brightest star in the sky. They will not urinate, defecate, spit, or blow their noses. Their combs are gold, their sweat is musk, their censers are aloes wood, their wives are the wide-eyed houris, their characters are the character of one man, and they are in the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall in the sky."

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Jarir.

Al-Zuhri said, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "A group of my nation will enter Paradise, seventy thousand of them, their faces shining like the moon on the night of the full moon." 'Ukkasha ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them." He (ﷺ) said: "'Ukkasha has outstripped you in this."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it. This hadith about the seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning has been narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Imran ibn Husayn, Ibn Mas'ud, Rifa'ah ibn 'Arabah al-Juhani, and Umm Qays bint Mihsan.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also have, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand of my nation, or seven hundred thousand, will enter Paradise, holding onto one another, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation into Paradise, with every thousand having seventy thousand, and there will be no reckoning or punishment for them, and three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Likewise, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated it from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Sulaym ibn 'Amir, and Abu al-Yaman 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Lahay, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tabarani narrated it.

Al-Tabarani also narrated, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami: "Then every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand."

The like of this has been narrated from Thawban and Abu Sa'id al-Anmari, and it has many supporting narrations from various routes.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Hatta idha ja'uha wa futihat abwabuha wa qala lahum khazanatuha salamun 'alaykum tibtum fadkhulluha khalidin﴾ (Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it to abide therein."), the answer is not mentioned here, and its implied meaning is: "Until, when they reach it," and these matters of opening the gates for them are an honour and a glorification. The keeping angels receive them with glad tidings, peace and praise, not as the torment-angels (al-Zabaniyah) receive the disbelievers with reproach and rebuke. So the implied meaning is: when this is the case, they will be happy and good, and joyful and delighted, to the degree of every pleasure they will have. When the answer is omitted here, the mind goes in every direction of hope and expectation.

As for those who claim that the "wa" in His saying ﴿wa futihat abwabuha﴾ is the waw al-thamaniyah (the "waw" of eight) and use it as evidence that the gates of Paradise are eight, they have gone too far and overreached. The fact that Paradise has eight gates is only learned from the authentic hadiths.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends two pairs of his wealth in the way of Allah will be called from the gates of Paradise. Paradise has gates: whoever is among the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer, whoever is among the people of charity will be called from the gate of charity, whoever is among the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad, and whoever is among the people of fasting will be called from the gate of al-Rayyan." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is no necessity for anyone to be called from any of them; but will anyone be called from all of them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, and I hope you will be among them."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri in similar wording.

In the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Abu Hazim Salamah ibn Dinar, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Paradise has eight gates, one of which is called al-Rayyan, which only those who fast will enter."

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you performs ablution and completes (or perfects) the ablution, then says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter by whichever he wishes."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The key to Paradise is: There is no god but Allah." Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad from the route of Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash; there is criticism of Shahr ibn Hawshab, and he did not hear from Mu'adh.

Mention of the vastness of the gates of Paradise. We ask Allah, the Mighty, of His bounty, to make us among its people:

In the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, in the long hadith of intercession: "Allah will say: 'O Muhammad, admit those from your nation who have no reckoning against them, from the right gate, and they are partners of the people in the other gates.' By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaves of the doors of Paradise, between the two doorposts, is like the distance between Mecca and Hajar, or Hajar and Mecca." In another narration: "Mecca and Busra."

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Utbah ibn Ghazwan, that he gave them a sermon in which he said: "It has been mentioned to us that the distance between the two leaves of the doors of Paradise is a forty years' journey, and a day will come upon it when it will be crowded to overflowing."

In al-Musnad, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the like of this.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the distance between the two leaves in Paradise is a forty years' journey." Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿wa qala lahum khazanatuha salamun 'alaykum tibtum﴾ (and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you are good"), this means: your deeds and your words were good, and your striving was good, so your reward is good. Just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that it be proclaimed among the Muslims during some of the battles: "Indeed, Paradise will not be entered except by a Muslim soul," and in another narration: "a believing soul." (Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah.)

* *

As for His saying: ﴿fadkhuluha khalidin﴾ (so enter it to abide therein), this means: remaining in it forever, not seeking any change from it.

**[Commentary of Ibn Kathir on Surah 39, verses 73–74, part 2]**

﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us."﴾ That is, the believers will say when they see, in Paradise, that abundant reward, that great bounty, that everlasting bliss and that vast dominion, and they will say at that moment: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾, meaning the One who promised us through the tongues of His noble messengers, just as they had supplicated in the world: ﴿Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 194]. ﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has guided us to this. We could not have been guided if Allah had not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth."﴾ [al-A'raf: 43]. ﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has removed from us all grief. Indeed, our Lord is All-Forgiving and Most Appreciative, who has settled us, by His bounty, in the abode of permanence. Therein no fatigue touches us, nor does weariness touch us."﴾ [Fatir: 34–35].

* *

As for their saying: ﴿And He has caused us to inherit the land, to settle in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾ Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Salih, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd [in (T): "and Abu Salih and others"] said: that is, the land of Paradise.

This verse is like His saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105]. Hence they said: ﴿to settle in Paradise wherever we will﴾, meaning: wherever we wish, we will dwell; so excellent is the reward, our reward for our deeds.

In the Sahihayn [al-Bukhari and Muslim], from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Anas, in the account of the Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension) [technical term: Mi'raj, the ascension of the Prophet ﷺ through the heavens], the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was admitted into Paradise, and there I saw domes of pearls, and its soil was musk." [Note: see the full hadith at the commentary on the first verse of Surah al-Isra'.]

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id [may Allah be pleased with him] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Ibn Sa'id about the soil of Paradise. He said: "White flour, pure musk." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken the truth."

Muslim also related it from the hadith of Abu Maslamah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with the same wording. [Note: al-Muntakhab, no. 874; Sahih Muslim, no. 2928.]

Muslim also related it [also] from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Abu Usamah, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id: that Ibn Sayyad asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the soil of Paradise, and he said: "White flour, pure musk." [Note: Sahih Muslim, no. 2928.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damrah [in (T): "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from 'Ali"; in (A): "Hamzah"], from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups﴾. He said: They will be driven until they reach a gate of the gates of Paradise, where they will find a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. They will head towards one of them and purify themselves with it, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them, so their skins will never be altered afterward and their hair will never become disheveled afterward, as though they had been anointed with oil. Then they will head towards the other, as though they had been commanded to, and drink from it, and it will cleanse whatever was in their bellies of impurity or filth. The angels will receive them at the gates of Paradise: ﴿Peace be upon you; you have been good, so enter it, abiding forever.﴾ Each of them will meet his servant boys, who will surround him like children greeting a beloved one returning from absence, saying: "Rejoice, Allah has prepared for you such and such honor, Allah has prepared for you such and such honor."

He also said: A servant boy of his will go to his wives among the wide-eyed houris, and say: "This is so-and-so," by his name in the world, and they will say: "Did you see him?" He will say: "Yes." Joy will so overwhelm them that they will rush out to the threshold of the door. He said: He will come and find couches arranged, cups set out, and carpets spread. He said: Then he will look at the foundation of his building, and find it founded on a bed of pearls, of red, green, yellow [and white] [in (T), (S), (A): added], and of every color. Then he will raise his gaze to its ceiling, and were it not that Allah had decreed it for him, it would nearly take away his sight; it is like lightning. Then he will look at his wives among the wide-eyed houris, then he will recline on one of his couches, and then he will say: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has guided us to this. We could not have been guided if Allah had not guided us.﴾ [al-A'raf: 43], and so on.

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi narrated to us, Maslamah [in (T), (A): "Salamah"] ibn Ja'far al-Bajali narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Basri say: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was one day with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves, they will be brought (or: they will be brought) on she-camels with wings, upon which are saddles of gold; the straps of their sandals are light that shines, and every step of theirs spans as far as the eye can see. They will come to a tree from whose root two springs gush forth. They will drink from one of them, and whatever was in their bellies of impurity will be washed away, and they will bathe in the other, and their skins will never become disheveled afterward, nor their hair, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them. Then they will come (or: arrive) at the gate of Paradise, and there is a ring of red ruby upon sheets of gold. They will strike the ring against the plate, and its resonance will be heard, O 'Ali. It will reach every wide-eyed houri that her husband has come, and she will send her guardian, who will open for him. When he sees him, he will fall down before him prostrate. [Maslamah said: I think he said: prostrate.] He will say: 'Raise your head, for I am only your guardian, appointed over your affair.' He will follow him and go in his footsteps, and the houri will be overtaken by haste, and will come out from tents of pearl and ruby until she embraces him, and then she will say: 'You are my beloved, and I am your beloved. I am the everlasting one who does not die; I am the blissful one who is never miserable; I am the content one who is never angry; and I am the abiding one who never departs.'" Then he will enter a house whose length from its foundation to its roof is one hundred thousand cubits, built upon a bed of pearls, with streaks of yellow, green and red, no streak resembling its companion. In the house are seventy couches, upon each couch seventy cushions, upon each cushion seventy wives, and upon each wife seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin can be seen through the garments. He will have intercourse with her for a duration equal to one night of your nights here. The rivers will flow beneath them: rivers of water unspoiled [he said: clear, with no turbidity in it], rivers of milk whose taste never changes [he said: it has not come out of the udders of livestock], rivers of wine, a delight for drinkers [he said: men have not pressed it with their feet], and rivers of pure honey [he said: it has not come out of the bellies of bees]. He will pluck the fruits, whether standing, sitting or reclining as he wishes." Then he recited: ﴿And its shade will be near over them, and its clusters will be lowered to within easy reach.﴾ [al-Insan: 14]. "He will desire food, and a white bird will come to him" [he said: and perhaps he said: green]. He said: "It will spread its wings, and he will eat from its sides whatever color he wishes. Then it will fly away and depart. Then an angel will enter and say: 'Peace be upon you. This is the Paradise you have been given as inheritance for what you used to do.' And if a single hair from the hair of a wide-eyed houri were to fall upon the people of the earth, the sun would be lit with its darkness in light."

This is a gharib (strange) hadith, and it appears to be mursal (one whose chain drops a companion), and Allah knows best.

This is a report about the state of the righteous believers when they are driven to Paradise in groups, mounted on noble she-camels. ﴿Zumaran﴾ means groups following one after another: first the closest ones (al-Muqarrabun), then the righteous (al-Abrar), then those who come after them. Each group goes with those similar to them: the prophets with the prophets, the truthful (al-Siddiqun) with their peers, the martyrs with their like, and the scholars with their equals. Every category goes with its own kind, and each group suits the others.

﴿Hatta idha ja'uha﴾ means that when they reach the gates of Paradise, after crossing the Sirat, they are held back on a bridge between Paradise and Hellfire. Wrongs that existed between them in the world are settled for them. When they have been purified and cleansed, they are given permission to enter Paradise. A hadith about the Trumpet (hadith al-Suwar) reports that when the believers reach the gates of Paradise, they consult among themselves about who should ask permission for them to enter. They go to Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, then Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, just as they did in the places of standing (al-'Arasat) when they asked for intercession with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He come to judge, so that the nobility of Muhammad (ﷺ) over all mankind might be made manifest in all these situations.

It is firmly established in Sahih Muslim, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the first intercessor in Paradise." In another wording in Muslim: "And I am the first to knock on the door of Paradise."

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us, Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will come to the gate of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection and ask for it to be opened. The gatekeeper will say: 'Who are you?' I will say: 'Muhammad.' He will say: 'It was commanded to me that I must not open it for anyone before you.'"

Muslim also narrated it from Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb, both from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Sulayman, who is Ibn al-Mughira al-Qaysi, from Thabit, from Anas, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first group to enter Paradise will have faces like the moon on the night of the full moon. They will not spit in it, nor blow their noses in it, nor defecate in it. Their vessels and combs will be of gold and silver, their censers will be of aloes wood, their sweat will be musk, and each of them will have two wives, through whose flesh the marrow of their shins can be seen because of their beauty. There will be no disagreement among them and no hatred; their hearts will be as one heart, and they will glorify Allah morning and evening."

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Muqatil, from Ibn al-Mubarak. Muslim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafi', from 'Abd al-Razzaq, both from Ma'mar with its chain, in similar wording. Likewise, Abu al-Zinad narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Khaythama narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those who follow them will be in the light of the brightest star in the sky. They will not urinate, defecate, spit, or blow their noses. Their combs are gold, their sweat is musk, their censers are aloes wood, their wives are the wide-eyed houris, their characters are the character of one man, and they are in the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall in the sky."

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Jarir.

Al-Zuhri said, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "A group of my nation will enter Paradise, seventy thousand of them, their faces shining like the moon on the night of the full moon." 'Ukkasha ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He make me one of them." He (ﷺ) said: "'Ukkasha has outstripped you in this."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it. This hadith about the seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning has been narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Imran ibn Husayn, Ibn Mas'ud, Rifa'ah ibn 'Arabah al-Juhani, and Umm Qays bint Mihsan.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also have, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand of my nation, or seven hundred thousand, will enter Paradise, holding onto one another, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation into Paradise, with every thousand having seventy thousand, and there will be no reckoning or punishment for them, and three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Likewise, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated it from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Sulaym ibn 'Amir, and Abu al-Yaman 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Lahay, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tabarani narrated it.

Al-Tabarani also narrated, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami: "Then every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand."

The like of this has been narrated from Thawban and Abu Sa'id al-Anmari, and it has many supporting narrations from various routes.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Hatta idha ja'uha wa futihat abwabuha wa qala lahum khazanatuha salamun 'alaykum tibtum fadkhulluha khalidin﴾ (Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it to abide therein."), the answer is not mentioned here, and its implied meaning is: "Until, when they reach it," and these matters of opening the gates for them are an honour and a glorification. The keeping angels receive them with glad tidings, peace and praise, not as the torment-angels (al-Zabaniyah) receive the disbelievers with reproach and rebuke. So the implied meaning is: when this is the case, they will be happy and good, and joyful and delighted, to the degree of every pleasure they will have. When the answer is omitted here, the mind goes in every direction of hope and expectation.

As for those who claim that the "wa" in His saying ﴿wa futihat abwabuha﴾ is the waw al-thamaniyah (the "waw" of eight) and use it as evidence that the gates of Paradise are eight, they have gone too far and overreached. The fact that Paradise has eight gates is only learned from the authentic hadiths.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends two pairs of his wealth in the way of Allah will be called from the gates of Paradise. Paradise has gates: whoever is among the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer, whoever is among the people of charity will be called from the gate of charity, whoever is among the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad, and whoever is among the people of fasting will be called from the gate of al-Rayyan." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is no necessity for anyone to be called from any of them; but will anyone be called from all of them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, and I hope you will be among them."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri in similar wording.

In the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Abu Hazim Salamah ibn Dinar, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Paradise has eight gates, one of which is called al-Rayyan, which only those who fast will enter."

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you performs ablution and completes (or perfects) the ablution, then says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter by whichever he wishes."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The key to Paradise is: There is no god but Allah." Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad from the route of Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash; there is criticism of Shahr ibn Hawshab, and he did not hear from Mu'adh.

Mention of the vastness of the gates of Paradise. We ask Allah, the Mighty, of His bounty, to make us among its people:

In the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, in the long hadith of intercession: "Allah will say: 'O Muhammad, admit those from your nation who have no reckoning against them, from the right gate, and they are partners of the people in the other gates.' By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaves of the doors of Paradise, between the two doorposts, is like the distance between Mecca and Hajar, or Hajar and Mecca." In another narration: "Mecca and Busra."

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Utbah ibn Ghazwan, that he gave them a sermon in which he said: "It has been mentioned to us that the distance between the two leaves of the doors of Paradise is a forty years' journey, and a day will come upon it when it will be crowded to overflowing."

In al-Musnad, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the like of this.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the distance between the two leaves in Paradise is a forty years' journey." Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿wa qala lahum khazanatuha salamun 'alaykum tibtum﴾ (and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you are good"), this means: your deeds and your words were good, and your striving was good, so your reward is good. Just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that it be proclaimed among the Muslims during some of the battles: "Indeed, Paradise will not be entered except by a Muslim soul," and in another narration: "a believing soul." (Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah.)

* *

As for His saying: ﴿fadkhuluha khalidin﴾ (so enter it to abide therein), this means: remaining in it forever, not seeking any change from it.

**[Commentary of Ibn Kathir on Surah 39, verses 73–74, part 2]**

﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us."﴾ That is, the believers will say when they see, in Paradise, that abundant reward, that great bounty, that everlasting bliss and that vast dominion, and they will say at that moment: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾, meaning the One who promised us through the tongues of His noble messengers, just as they had supplicated in the world: ﴿Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 194]. ﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has guided us to this. We could not have been guided if Allah had not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth."﴾ [al-A'raf: 43]. ﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has removed from us all grief. Indeed, our Lord is All-Forgiving and Most Appreciative, who has settled us, by His bounty, in the abode of permanence. Therein no fatigue touches us, nor does weariness touch us."﴾ [Fatir: 34–35].

* *

As for their saying: ﴿And He has caused us to inherit the land, to settle in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾ Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Salih, Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd [in (T): "and Abu Salih and others"] said: that is, the land of Paradise.

This verse is like His saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105]. Hence they said: ﴿to settle in Paradise wherever we will﴾, meaning: wherever we wish, we will dwell; so excellent is the reward, our reward for our deeds.

In the Sahihayn [al-Bukhari and Muslim], from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Anas, in the account of the Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension) [technical term: Mi'raj, the ascension of the Prophet ﷺ through the heavens], the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was admitted into Paradise, and there I saw domes of pearls, and its soil was musk." [Note: see the full hadith at the commentary on the first verse of Surah al-Isra'.]

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id [may Allah be pleased with him] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Ibn Sa'id about the soil of Paradise. He said: "White flour, pure musk." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken the truth."

Muslim also related it from the hadith of Abu Maslamah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with the same wording. [Note: al-Muntakhab, no. 874; Sahih Muslim, no. 2928.]

Muslim also related it [also] from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Abu Usamah, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id: that Ibn Sayyad asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the soil of Paradise, and he said: "White flour, pure musk." [Note: Sahih Muslim, no. 2928.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damrah [in (T): "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from 'Ali"; in (A): "Hamzah"], from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups﴾. He said: They will be driven until they reach a gate of the gates of Paradise, where they will find a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. They will head towards one of them and purify themselves with it, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them, so their skins will never be altered afterward and their hair will never become disheveled afterward, as though they had been anointed with oil. Then they will head towards the other, as though they had been commanded to, and drink from it, and it will cleanse whatever was in their bellies of impurity or filth. The angels will receive them at the gates of Paradise: ﴿Peace be upon you; you have been good, so enter it, abiding forever.﴾ Each of them will meet his servant boys, who will surround him like children greeting a beloved one returning from absence, saying: "Rejoice, Allah has prepared for you such and such honor, Allah has prepared for you such and such honor."

He also said: A servant boy of his will go to his wives among the wide-eyed houris, and say: "This is so-and-so," by his name in the world, and they will say: "Did you see him?" He will say: "Yes." Joy will so overwhelm them that they will rush out to the threshold of the door. He said: He will come and find couches arranged, cups set out, and carpets spread. He said: Then he will look at the foundation of his building, and find it founded on a bed of pearls, of red, green, yellow [and white] [in (T), (S), (A): added], and of every color. Then he will raise his gaze to its ceiling, and were it not that Allah had decreed it for him, it would nearly take away his sight; it is like lightning. Then he will look at his wives among the wide-eyed houris, then he will recline on one of his couches, and then he will say: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has guided us to this. We could not have been guided if Allah had not guided us.﴾ [al-A'raf: 43], and so on.

Then he said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi narrated to us, Maslamah [in (T), (A): "Salamah"] ibn Ja'far al-Bajali narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Basri say: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was one day with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves, they will be brought (or: they will be brought) on she-camels with wings, upon which are saddles of gold; the straps of their sandals are light that shines, and every step of theirs spans as far as the eye can see. They will come to a tree from whose root two springs gush forth. They will drink from one of them, and whatever was in their bellies of impurity will be washed away, and they will bathe in the other, and their skins will never become disheveled afterward, nor their hair, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them. Then they will come (or: arrive) at the gate of Paradise, and there is a ring of red ruby upon sheets of gold. They will strike the ring against the plate, and its resonance will be heard, O 'Ali. It will reach every wide-eyed houri that her husband has come, and she will send her guardian, who will open for him. When he sees him, he will fall down before him prostrate. [Maslamah said: I think he said: prostrate.] He will say: 'Raise your head, for I am only your guardian, appointed over your affair.' He will follow him and go in his footsteps, and the houri will be overtaken by haste, and will come out from tents of pearl and ruby until she embraces him, and then she will say: 'You are my beloved, and I am your beloved. I am the everlasting one who does not die; I am the blissful one who is never miserable; I am the content one who is never angry; and I am the abiding one who never departs.'" Then he will enter a house whose length from its foundation to its roof is one hundred thousand cubits, built upon a bed of pearls, with streaks of yellow, green and red, no streak resembling its companion. In the house are seventy couches, upon each couch seventy cushions, upon each cushion seventy wives, and upon each wife seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin can be seen through the garments. He will have intercourse with her for a duration equal to one night of your nights here. The rivers will flow beneath them: rivers of water unspoiled [he said: clear, with no turbidity in it], rivers of milk whose taste never changes [he said: it has not come out of the udders of livestock], rivers of wine, a delight for drinkers [he said: men have not pressed it with their feet], and rivers of pure honey [he said: it has not come out of the bellies of bees]. He will pluck the fruits, whether standing, sitting or reclining as he wishes." Then he recited: ﴿And its shade will be near over them, and its clusters will be lowered to within easy reach.﴾ [al-Insan: 14]. "He will desire food, and a white bird will come to him" [he said: and perhaps he said: green]. He said: "It will spread its wings, and he will eat from its sides whatever color he wishes. Then it will fly away and depart. Then an angel will enter and say: 'Peace be upon you. This is the Paradise you have been given as inheritance for what you used to do.' And if a single hair from the hair of a wide-eyed houri were to fall upon the people of the earth, the sun would be lit with its darkness in light."

This is a gharib (strange) hadith, and it appears to be mursal (one whose chain drops a companion), and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 39, verse 75:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned His judgment concerning the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and that He places each in the station that befits and suits them, and He is the Just in this, who does not oppress, He informed about His angels that they surround His glorious Throne, glorifying (yusabbihuna, tasbih) the praise of their Lord, and extolling Him (yumajjidunahu), and magnifying Him (yu'azzimunahu) and sanctifying Him (yuqaddisunahu) and declaring Him free from deficiencies and injustice. [In A: "wa-yahmadunahu" ("and praising Him").] He has settled the matter, decreed the affair, and judged with justice. For this reason He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, i.e., between the creatures, ﴿with truth﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ i.e., the speech of the entire universe, both its speaking and its dumb creatures, is "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds," praising Him for His judgment and His justice. For this reason He did not attribute the saying to any specific speaker but left it unrestricted, which indicates that all creation bears witness to His being praised.

Qatadah said: "He opened creation with praise in His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1], and concluded it with praise in His saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, 'All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'﴾"

End of the tafsir of Surah az-Zumar. And all praise is due to Allah [first and last, outwardly and inwardly]. [In A: "And Allah knows best."] [Addition from S.]
